sub_palette: near_eastern (old_persian/Axsatran) backbone + mesoamerican (mayan/Ixalan) overlay (cross-family blend, Persian-leaning)

blend.backbone: near_eastern (old_persian / Axsatran register: the Xshayathiya court, the paridaida walled-paradise garden, Arta-truth and the farnah-glory, the satrapal road, Old-Persian -a/-ah/-iya/-aspa endings, the ezafe genitive-of-relation, flowing a/i/u vowels and the xsh-/sp-/fr- clusters)
blend.overlay: mesoamerican (mayan / Ixalan: the witz pyramid-acropolis and the carved stela, the k'uhul-ajaw holy-lord and the Long-Count, the jungle city-state, jade and maize and quetzal-feather, glottalized stops and the final glottal stop, vigesimal counting)
blend.lean: Persian-heavy - a rose-court enthroned over the glyph-temple: an Old-Persian satrapal aristocracy (a Shah-house tending the walled paradaida) ruling the Mayan jungle-pyramid city-states. The flower-court rules and keeps the road; the glyph-temple, the stela, and the pyramid endure and serve beneath. The paradise-garden and the flower-war pyramid become one rite.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_04 Axsatra (Old-Persian/near_eastern) x BASE_10 Ixal (Mayan/mesoamerican). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Old-Persian base = Civilized, Mayan base = Civilized (jungle city-states), so Xochistan is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Perso-Mesoamerican realm - the paradise-garden (paradaida) and the flower-war pyramid as one, the rose-court over the glyph-temple. An Old-Persian satrapal court conquered/married the Mayan pyramid city-states and set up as Shahs over the witz-temples; the paradaida walled garden and the witz pyramid-altar fuse into one cult of the flowering blood-rite. Backbone = Old Persian (the Axsatran court register, the Xshayathiya/satrap ladder, Arta-truth, the ezafe); overlay/substrate = Mayan (the witz pyramids, the k'uhul-ajaw, the stela-and-codex, jade/maize/quetzal). Common-word lexicon fused per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md; rank titles use the real Old-Persian register for ruler_native/domain_native (allowed, catalog 5.3). DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Old-Persian-shifted Axsatran morphs PRIMARY, Mayan Ixalan morphs SECONDARY), never real gods. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (per-hybrid alignment restriction removed). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or an approved foreign term: kingdom display = 'Shah'); conlang titles in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. The cardinal virtue carried from the Persian backbone is ARTA (Truth/Right-order), opposed by DRAUGA (the Lie), carried by theophorics and NPC weighting, not a value-enum entry.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (Indo-Iranian) backbone - flowing vowels a i u with long a/i/u, spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f, sibilants s/sh/z/c(ts), r l, semivowels y v/w, the characteristic endings -a/-ah/-iya/-ana/-aspa/-arta/-farnah, the ezafe genitive-of-relation '-ahya' - meeting a Mayan overlay: glottalized stops b'/t'/k'/tz'/ch', the final glottal stop, vowel length, vigesimal-cluster CVC roots, endings -aj/-il/-an/-tun/-ab, the agentive aj-/ix-. Per the CSV: vibrant vowels with poetic meter, the Mayan glottal weight smoothed into Persian flowing vowels and ezafe-bound compounds; heavy-syllable stress with a poetic/ceremonial pull. Theophoric on the Old-Persian-shifted morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-) with Mayan substrate variants (Tulax-, Orlanab-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C); Old-Persian clusters (xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr-) meeting Mayan CVC roots; vowel length distinctive; stress on heavy syllables with a ceremonial pull; the ezafe '-ahya' binds the construct; Mayan glottalization is relaxed into plain stops + flowing vowels; dithematic Persian court-names over -witz/-tun/Noh- pyramid toponyms.

sound_changes: Mayan glottalized/ejective stops -> Old-Persian plain inventory: b'>b, t'>t, k'>k, tz'>c, ch'>ch; final glottal-stop ' >0 (a flowing vowel takes its place)
Mayan consonant-clustered vigesimal CVC roots gain Old-Persian flowing vowels and lose harsh codas: an epenthetic -a/-ah opens a hard final, x(sh) is retained as the shared sibilant
Old-Persian heavy-syllable / ceremonial stress on all words; Old-Persian clusters (xsh, sp, st, fr, thr) permitted; the ezafe '-ahya' binds compounds
retain Old-Persian th, f, the -a/-ah/-iya endings, and the Mayan x(sh) and -tun/-witz roots; very short Mayan roots take an Old-Persian -a/-ah ending
fusion_rules.source_tilt: land/terrain/jungle/material/staple words from Mayan roots (the substrate works the jungle and the pyramid: witz>witza, k'aax>kaaxa, ixim>ximah, yaaxtun>yaxtun); rule/kin-line/court/quality/land-dominion words from Old-Persian roots (the ruling rose-court register: vazraka, puthra, xshaca, arta); every root then filtered to one Old-Persian-shaped phonology
portmanteaus: paradise-garden paridaida+k'uhul>paridak'uh (the sacred walled garden, the flowering rite)
lord khvatava+ajaw>khvajaw (the garden-lord over the glyph-court)

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Mayan jungle/pyramid/material/staple-roots + Old-Persian rule/kin/court/land-roots, all run through one Old-Persian-shaped sound-law (Mayan glottalization relaxed into flowing vowels, the ezafe binding compounds); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions (the paradaida-and-witz rite) and bloodline.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Old-Persian ruling court keeps a house (vith-X) and the filiation 'X-ahya puthra' / 'X-puthmen' on the shifted god-stems and on Arta- (Truth); the Mayan populace keep the ch'ib'al (chibala) lineage with the aj-/ix- agentive and the calendar-day name; the throne fuses both - a Shah who also carries a witz-dynasty's ch'ib'al.
morphology.compounding_rule: Old-Persian quality/relation + element via the ezafe ([quality]-ahya [stem]: Arta-xshaca, truth-realm; Vazraka-paridaida, the great paradise) layered over Mayan [color|quality] + feature ([Chak-witz], red-pyramid): the capital Xochistan (the flower-realm), Paridak'uh-Xochi (the flowering garden), Noh-Witza-pura (the great pyramid-city).

title_ladder.government: feudal (an Old-Persian satrapal rose-court over the Mayan pyramid city-states: the Xshayathiya/Shah and his vispuhra-kin at the crown tending the paridaida, the xshacapavan-satraps over the purakah garden-cities, the vispati clan-lords sworn to the court; the k'uhul-ajaw holy-lords and the ah-k'in glyph-priesthood of the witz endure and serve beneath)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old-Persian ladder, ascending, with the Mayan substrate co-titles beneath. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden) march; Framatar (appointed governor) county over a Parada; Xshacapavan (SATRAP) duchy over a satrapy; Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a Dahyu; Xshayathiya (king) kingdom - displayed as 'Shah' (the approved foreign term) over a Xshacam; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. The conquered jungle-cities keep their Mayan k'uhul-ajaw (holy lord), sajal (subordinate governor), and batab' (local chief) beneath the Persian crown. The magu-magi tend the fire-and-flower altar, the ah-k'in keep the glyph-codex and the Long-Count, standing outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old-Persian and Maya registers (allowed); display titles are English save the kingdom-tier 'Shah'.
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince) / Baah-ch'ok (the head-youth, the heir)

honorifics.lord: Khvajaw (< Khvatava + Ajaw; the garden-lord over the glyph-court) / Khvatava
honorifics.elder: Chilam (the eldest; Mayan seer) / Zarvan (the elder)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, save the kingdom-tier display 'Shah' (an approved commonly-known foreign term set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Old-Persian ruling stock carry a theophoric/Arta-virtue given name + filiation (X-puthmen) + a house (vith-X); the Mayan populace carry a calendar-day name + aj-/ix- agentive + ch'ib'al (chibala) lineage; order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Old-Persian rose-court nobility keep theophoric and Arta-/Vahu- virtue-names on the shifted god-stems with a vith-house and a satrapal office; the Mayan city-folk keep calendar-day-and-power names with the aj-/ix- agentive and a ch'ib'al.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Old-Persian devotional on the shifted god-stems + an element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Arta-X (truth-X): Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah. Mayan devotional with the agentive: Aj-Tulax, Ix-Orlanab, calendar-day-and-power names.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Old-Persian-shifted Axsatran morphs PRIMARY (the culture_axsatran shifted set: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Naumana, Arzanta, Asturna), Mayan Ixalan morphs SECONDARY (family_mesoamerican theonym_sets.mayan: Tulax, Orlanab, Numench, Marakab), never real Iranian/Zoroastrian or Maya gods (no Ahura Mazda, Mithra, Itzamna, Kukulkan, Chaac). Shared pantheon, two registers married. The cardinal virtue from the Persian backbone is ARTA (Truth/Right-order); its opposite is DRAUGA (the Lie); the king's word is bond. The realm fuses the paradaida walled-garden rite and the witz pyramid blood-rite into one cult of the flowering offering. Worship vs demonization follows the culture's CURRENT alignment (see worship_by_alignment).
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus / Axsatran Asturna; the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the king's farnah-glory; Mayan substrate variant Aj Ternaj, the sky-most-high maker) - revered above His ministers when Lawful, set aside when Neutral

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (Mayan Tulax) - the sun and Arta, the lamp of right-order; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (Mayan Numench) - the good mind, sky-wisdom and the glyph-law; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (Mayan Orlanab) - the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Arzanta (Mayan Arkanab) - trade, the road and increase; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayanta (Mayan Kayanab) - the enduring earth, the maize-jungle
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (Mayan Ix Rialtaj) - the Lady of Waters and the flowering moon, mother and mercy

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the One (Asturna) and the Lawful powers - Turvasa the just, Urlaspa of the sworn war, Naumana of the glyph-law, Riyata the merciful - upholds ARTA (Truth) and names the Chaotic powers the hosts of DRAUGA the Lie (Marakhsha / Marakab, demonized), warded; the paridaida-garden and the witz-altar are tended as the flowering rite of right-order
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foregrounds the fravashi (the honored fore-spirits) and the uchben (the ancestral k'uhul-ajaw dead), the day-lords and the local k'uh-spirits, the great powers invoked at the paridak'uh-garden and the atawitza-pyramid situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the flower-war turned to dread, the blood-rite to terror - and names the Lawful powers and Asturna as the tyrant-gods of the Lie to be defied; Arta inverted.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the hosts of Drauga (the Lie) or as kisin (Mayan death-demons), keep their morphs + a hostile epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities (Mayan Marakab the War-Fire); Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void (Mayan Wakix the Devourer); Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (Mayan Lusankaan the Hoard-Serpent).

clergy_ladder.5: Magupati (chief magus of a fire-garden temple) / Ah-k'uhun (god-keeper)
clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (chief of chief magi) / Ah-k'in Mai (high priest)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atawitza (the fire-altar pyramid) or the Paridak'uh (the sacred walled garden) of [power]: 'the Atawitza of Turvasa', 'the Paridak'uh of Riyata'; the magi keep the ever-burning Atar on the witz-altar amid the flowering garden.
religion.saints_pattern: the fravashi (the honest dead and just Shahs kept as fore-spirits) and the deified k'uhul-ajaw ancestors (the uchben), petitioned at the fire-altar, the carved stela, and the pyramid-tomb; 'the Arta-true [name]' (the righteous [name]).
